question.prompt: Menkara has a \(4 \times 6\) index card. If she shortens the length of one side of this card by \(1\) inch, the card would have area \(18\) square inches. What would the area of the card be in square inches if instead she shortens the length of the other side by \(1\) inch?

solutions.title: Identify the shortened dimension
solutions.explanation:
Shortening the \(4\)-inch dimension gives a \(3\times6\) card with area \(3\cdot6=18\) square inches, so this is the change described in the condition.

Shortening the other dimension instead gives a \(4\times5\) card. Its area is
\[
4(6-1)=4\cdot5=\boxed{20}
\]
square inches, choice \(\text{(E)}\).
